title: [FEATURE] Detect a running compression proxy and route the observer through it
body:
The observer spawns a separate `claude` subprocess per `PostToolUse` and can carry up to 400 000 characters of conversation context (`CLAUDE_MEM_OBSERVER_MAX_CONVERSATION_CHARS`). When a local compression proxy is running — in my case Headroom on `127.0.0.1:8787`, which the host agent already routes through — those observer calls **bypass it entirely** and bill straight against the subscription's inference allowance.

On my machine that allowance ran out on 2026-09-11. `observer-health.json` recorded `"lastErrorKind": "quota_exhausted"`, and eleven observations titled *"Memory Observer Inference Allowance Exhausted"* ended up stored as knowledge. Because the SessionStart block is recency-ordered, 12 of the 17 entries shown at the next session start were those error messages — the system's own failure crowding out the content it exists to surface.

### The fix on my side was a single line

```
# ~/.claude-mem/.env
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787
```

`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is already in the env allowlist in `worker-service.cjs`, so it reaches the SDK subprocess without any code change. The file just isn't pre-populated, and nothing hints that it could be.

**Verified after the change**, on plugin 13.24.23 with a first-party OAuth login:

- observer subprocess environment contains the base URL (`/proc/<pid>/environ` of the spawned `claude --model claude-haiku-4-5-…` process)
- observations continue to be generated and stored — ids 563, 564, 565, 566, 567 after the switch, no auth failure
- `discovery_tokens` remain populated: 5/5 non-zero after the change, matching 562/562 before

That last check is aimed at #3664, which reported `discovery_tokens` always 0 via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateways — I could not reproduce that here.

Worth noting for anyone verifying this: **checking the proxy's model distribution is not sufficient evidence**, because the host agent issues Haiku calls of its own. The subprocess environment is the reliable signal.

### Relation to existing issues

- **#3778** (closed) reported the opposite failure — the spawned subprocess reporting *"Not logged in"* behind a proxy. That configuration also had `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in the settings env block. On the current version with OAuth only, I see no auth problem at all.
- **#3607** (open, Observer Subprocess Isolation) covers explicit env/auth handling for the headless generator; this request would fit naturally there if you prefer to fold it in.

### Suggestion

Probe `127.0.0.1:8787/health` — or a configurable address — at worker startup and adopt `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` when a proxy answers, with an opt-out setting. Failing that, a line in the docs would already help: the interaction is completely invisible until the quota runs out, and the failure then gets recorded as a memory.

*Investigated together with Claude Code (Opus 5).*

title: fix(worker): refresh all quota windows from unifiedWindows, drop reset snapshots
body:
Refs #4068 · Refs #3870

## Problem

`RateLimitStore.set()` stores each `rate_limit_event` only under its binding `rateLimitType`, which is almost always `five_hour`. The `seven_day` bucket gets written only by the rare event whose binding window is `seven_day`, and entries never expire. So one high `seven_day` reading stays in worker memory for the life of the process. `shouldAbortForQuota` keeps tripping on it, and the persisted quota cooldown gets re-armed on every restart.

Reproduced on 13.24.23 after switching Claude Code to a different account:

- The store held `seven_day` at `utilization: 0.98` from the previous account, with `resetsAt` still ~4 days in the future.
- Every live event from the new account was keyed `five_hour` and reported, in the same payload, `unifiedWindows.seven_day.utilization: 0.24`.
- The observer aborted on every request (`quota:seven_day utilization 98.0% >= 93%`) until the process was replaced.

An expiry check alone would **not** have fixed this case, because `resetsAt` hadn't passed yet. The fix has to take the fresh reading that is already in every event.

A live payload, trimmed:

```json
{"status":"allowed","resetsAt":1789249800,"rateLimitType":"five_hour",
 "overageStatus":"rejected","isUsingOverage":false,
 "unifiedWindows":{"five_hour":{"utilization":0.04,"resetsAt":1789249800},
                   "seven_day":{"utilization":0.01,"resetsAt":1789563600}}}
```

Two details in this payload matter:

- The top-level payload has no `utilization`. It only appears inside `unifiedWindows`.
- `resetsAt` is epoch **seconds**, not the ms the SDK docs describe. `minutesUntilReset` already handles this.

## Change (`src/services/worker/RateLimitStore.ts`)

- **`set()`:** fans `unifiedWindows` out to the per-window buckets, so windows that are never the binding one stay current. A fresh reading replaces a stale `rejected` snapshot. The binding window's `utilization` is backfilled from the same map when the top-level payload omits it. The return value (new-rejection signal) is unchanged: it still reflects only the binding window.
- **`get(type, now)`:** returns `undefined` once a snapshot's `resetsAt` has passed. `shouldAbortForQuota` passes its `now` through, and `getMostRecentByWindow()` (the health surface) now goes through `get()`.
- **`toEpochMs()`:** one seconds-vs-ms normalizer, used by `minutesUntilReset`, the expiry check and the `five_hour` reset-grace check. The grace check used to compute `entry.resetsAt - now` directly. With live second-based values that is always hugely negative, so the grace buffer never fired.

The thresholds, the API-key bypass and the ordering are all unchanged.

## Tests (`tests/worker/rate-limit-store.test.ts`)

Eight new cases:

- the account-switch case (stale `seven_day` 0.98 with `resetsAt` in the future, then a live event with `seven_day` 0.24 → no abort)
- a hot control (`unifiedWindows.seven_day` 0.95 → still aborts on `seven_day`)
- the binding window's own `rejected` status is kept
- an explicit top-level utilization wins over the `unifiedWindows` copy
- malformed `unifiedWindows` is ignored
- expiry works for both seconds and ms
- the reset grace fires for second-based `resetsAt`

```
bun test tests/worker/rate-limit-store.test.ts
  main + new tests:  44 pass, 5 fail   (the 5 new behavior tests fail)
  this branch:       49 pass, 0 fail
```

`tsc --noEmit` is clean. Across all 11 test files that reference the store or `ClaudeProvider`, the results are the same as on `main` except for the new cases. The one remaining failure, `logger-usage-standards`, also fails on `main` on Windows; it flags `console.*` calls in unrelated `src\npx-cli\` files.

## Not in this PR

#4068 also reports that queued observations are lost across a restart during a cooldown. That is a separate defect and is not addressed here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Feature Request] Add configurable observer batching at summary or session end to reduce token usage
body:
## Summary

Add an option to defer claude-mem’s observer model work until a summary boundary or session close, instead of processing observations at the current high-frequency cadence. This would let users reduce background token use while retaining automatic memory capture.

The [hook lifecycle documentation](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/blob/main/docs/public/architecture/hooks.mdx) describes `PostToolUse` as queueing observations for AI compression and `Stop` as triggering a summary. `Stop` can occur while a session is still active; `SessionEnd` marks the session complete. The [configuration docs](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration) document tool exclusions, but I found no setting for observation frequency, batching, or a token budget.

## Anonymized usage evidence

These are locally aggregated transcript counters. “Raw token total” below means the sum of logged input, cache-read input, cache-creation input, and output tokens; it is not a cost estimate or a percentage of plan capacity.

- **Window:** 2026-09-12 21:52Z to 2026-09-13 01:52Z (4 hours). The preceding hour had no model calls, so the five-hour comparison window had the same logged total.
- **All observed traffic:** 18,148,270 raw tokens across 248 model responses.
- **claude-mem observer:** 7,866,510 raw tokens across 128 responses—**43.3%** of observed token traffic. The logged breakdown was 1,280 input, 0 cache-read, 7,618,468 cache-creation, and 246,762 output tokens.
- **Peak rolling hour:** 88 observer responses and approximately 6.13 million raw tokens.
- **Metadata:** claude-mem 13.24.23, Claude provider, Haiku model. The observer entered cooldown after the provider reported “inference allowance exhausted.”
- Hook metadata showed `PostToolUse` observation and `Stop` summary events in both Claude Code and Codex integrations. The aggregate token counters do **not** identify which host triggered each response.

The observed 43.3% is a share of logged token traffic, **not** a share of a five-hour plan quota; plan-capacity usage was not available in these local records.

## Proposed option

Add a documented setting, name provisional, such as:

```json
{
  "CLAUDE_MEM_OBSERVATION_TRIGGER": "per_observation"
}
```

Possible values:

- `per_observation` — current behavior and default for backwards compatibility.
- `on_summary` — buffer tool events until a summary boundary and combine observation extraction with that summary’s model request. Document that `Stop` may occur multiple times during a session.
- `on_session_end` — buffer events and process them once at the actual session-close event. This should be the mode for users who want one observer invocation per completed session.

The setting should change when model inference happens, not whether eligible tool events are captured locally. Preserve queued events across worker restarts and make normal session-close processing retry-safe. If a batch exceeds a configured size limit, document how it is bounded and report any truncation rather than silently losing events.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Existing installations retain current behavior unless the setting is changed.
2. In `on_summary` mode, queued observations are handled with the corresponding summary request, rather than a separate model request per event.
3. In `on_session_end` mode, a completed session causes at most one observer inference, excluding retries.
4. Queued observations survive worker restarts and are not duplicated when a close event is retried.
5. Existing memory search and context injection continue to work in both modes.
6. Logs or status output expose the selected mode and counts of queued events and observer inferences, so users can verify the reduction.

## Related reports

- [#1938](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues/1938) reports missing observer budget/frequency controls.
- [#2431](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues/2431) reports Claude-backed model work from Codex observation and summary hooks.
- [#2721](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues/2721) describes disabling write hooks as a workaround while retaining read-only context/search.

title: Chroma backfill reports completion during shutdown and counts empty rows as missing
body:
Found while re-syncing a rebuilt local Chroma index on 2026-09-12 (worker 13.24.23).

**What happens**
- When the worker stops mid-sweep, `stop()` closes the mutation gate while the background backfill keeps running. Every write then fails with "Local Chroma mutations are unavailable after shutdown begins", yet the sweep still logs `Smart backfill complete` per project and `Backfill check complete for all projects` at the end. Completion is reported for a cancelled run. (`src/services/sync/ChromaMcpManager.ts` around the stop path and write rejection; `src/services/worker-service.ts` global completion log.)
- `missing=rows.length` counts rows that produce zero documents (no narrative, text or facts). The loop skips them without advancing the watermark, so they are reported as missing on every pass and can never drain. (`src/services/sync/ChromaSync.ts` backfill loop and formatter.)
- The returned `totalDocs` is the number of planned documents, not successful writes.
- Project enumeration excludes prompts that cannot be joined to a session, so some rows are never candidates at all.

**Proposed fix**
- Propagate shutdown cancellation to the outer sweep and gate project/global completion on "no outstanding eligible rows", not on the promise resolving.
- Return written / empty / failed / aborted counts separately and classify empty rows so they stop being called missing.
- Enumerate the union of observation, summary and session-joined prompt projects, including empty project names.

Full read-only diagnosis with file:line citations is in the seat's notes; happy to attach on request.

— Prioritizer (seat for Alex, cmem.ai)

title: Quota guard aborts on a seven_day snapshot past its resetsAt (13.24.23), and the only workaround, restart, discards the in-memory queue
body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and confirmed this is not a duplicate

## Related

- **Defect 1 is a known bug, not a new one.** The stale-snapshot mechanism is #3870 (closed 2026-09-11, consolidated into #3606). The `seven_day` variant with an already-reset window is in the #3606 thread from @edgar-eaca (13.24.1), and @yhi264 reproduced the guard on 13.24.23 with `/api/health` snapshots. It is missing only from the #3606 plan text. The Defect 1 section below is one more 13.24.23 repro; please read it as corroboration of that thread.
- **Defect 2 is the part that is not tracked.** Queue loss on restart: #3813 was consolidated into #3603 (port/liveness), and #3609 describes a DB-backed `PendingMessageStore`. Neither matches the shipped build, where the observer queue lives only in memory. @yhi264 mentioned a discarded `pendingCount=160` in passing; the scale and the cause are below. Summary also posted in #3606: https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues/3606#issuecomment-5651781960

Filing separately because Defect 2 is not covered by any open issue, and the only recovery for Defect 1 is what triggers it.

## Bug description

Two defects that compound each other:

1. **The quota guard keeps aborting on a `seven_day` snapshot whose `resetsAt` is already in the past.** Memory capture stays off after the weekly window has reset, until the worker restarts.
2. **The only workaround, a graceful worker restart, silently discards every queued observation.** The queue lives only in process memory and the shutdown path neither drains nor persists it.

## Environment

- claude-mem **13.24.23** (bun daemon `scripts/worker-service.cjs`)
- Claude Code CLI 2.1.268, Claude desktop app 1.52386.3
- macOS 14.5 (Darwin 23.5.0), Bun 1.3.11
- Provider `claude`, auth: Claude Code OAuth token from keychain, subscription plan
- Observer model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`
- All times below are local, UTC+5

## Defect 1: stale `seven_day` snapshot outlives `resetsAt`

`GET /api/health` at 23:07, same worker process (up since the previous day):

```
seven_day  utilization=0.93  status=allowed_warning  observedAt=18:24:14  resetsAt=19:00:00
five_hour                    status=allowed          observedAt=22:53:24  resetsAt=03:20:00 (next day)
```

The weekly window reset at 19:00. Four hours later the guard still aborts on the entry observed at 18:24. Every cooldown probe gets a fresh `five_hour` event (`allowed`), then `shouldAbortForQuota` iterates all windows, hits the frozen `seven_day` entry and re-arms the 30 min cooldown:

```
[2026-09-12 22:52:49.757] [SESSION] Generator auto-starting (observation) using Claude SDK {queueDepth=150}
[2026-09-12 22:53:24.688] [SDK    ] ← Response received (715 chars) ⚠️ **CRITICAL: Memory Recording Disabled** The claude-mem allowance has been exhausted (since 2026-09-12T16:47:10.757Z) ...
[2026-09-12 22:53:24.691] [PARSER ] SDK returned non-XML prose response
[2026-09-12 22:53:24.693] [SDK    ] Aborting session for quota guard: quota:seven_day utilization 93.0% >= 93%
[2026-09-12 22:53:27.243] [SESSION] Generator paused for quota; preserving buffered work {pendingCount=122}
```

Every quota-guard abort in the log over two days reported exactly `93.0%`, never a different value. Meanwhile the desktop app's own usage indicator had already dropped the weekly warning.

**Corroborates the expired-window case already reported in #3606.** Here the frozen entry's `resetsAt` was 4 hours in the past, the same shape edgar-eaca reported for `seven_day` on 13.24.1 (window reset about 26 h earlier) and yhi264 for `five_hour` on 13.24.23. Together with andreiiliuta's case on #3870, where `resetsAt` was still in the future, this is one more sign that neither check is enough alone: expire on `resetsAt < now` with `resetsAt` normalised once in `set()` (a seconds-valued `resetsAt` would otherwise switch the guard off, as edgar-eaca found), and refresh sibling windows from `unifiedWindows`, which also has to clear a frozen `status: "rejected"` (yhi264's run 2).

State of `main` (`src/services/worker/RateLimitStore.ts`, last change 2026-09-11 for #3903): `unifiedWindows` 0 occurrences, `.delete(` / `.clear(` 0 occurrences, `observedAt` written but never read. The bundled 13.24.23 matches: one `set`, no eviction, and the threshold table `{five_hour:.95, seven_day_opus:.93, seven_day_sonnet:.92, seven_day:.93, overage:.95}` is compared without any `resetsAt` or age check.

Side note, still present on 13.24.23 (#3902 family): the 715-char response above is the observer paraphrasing claude-mem's own health banner, which it was fed. The parser drops it as prose, so even a probe that passes the guard wastes its first turn.

## Defect 2: restart discards the in-memory queue

Last status broadcast before the restart, then the whole shutdown sequence:

```
[2026-09-12 23:18:51.133] [WORKER  ] Broadcasting processing status {isProcessing=true, queueDepth=1297, activeSessions=11}
[2026-09-12 23:18:51.698] [SYSTEM  ] Shutdown initiated
[2026-09-12 23:18:51.707] [SHUTDOWN] Stopping Chroma MCP connection...
[2026-09-12 23:18:53.886] [SYSTEM  ] Worker shutdown complete
```

No drain, no persist step. Evidence that the 1297 queued events are gone rather than recovered:

- Last `ENQUEUED` on the old worker was `messageId=3562`; the first one on the new worker is `messageId=4`, so the id counter is per-process.
- `pending_messages` has 0 rows after the restart, and the 13.24.23 bundle contains no `INSERT ... INTO pending_messages` at all (case-insensitive search), so nothing writes queued work to SQLite.
- The new worker's startup log has no recovery lines, only `Discarding stale memory_session_id from previous worker instance (Issue #817)`.
- Between the last successful `STORED` (21:47:08) and the shutdown (23:18:51) there were **602 `ENQUEUED` events across 6 sessions in 5 projects**. None of them produced observations.

Raw transcripts still exist, but there is no replay path: `POST /api/import` accepts ready observations, and `transcript-watcher` only tails new lines.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the observer on a subscription account until a `rate_limit_event` with `rateLimitType: seven_day` and `utilization >= 0.93` arrives. The guard aborts correctly.
2. Wait past that event's `resetsAt` while the same worker process keeps running.
3. After each 30 min cooldown the probe is admitted, receives only a `five_hour` event and aborts again on `quota:seven_day utilization 93.0%`. `/api/health` shows `seven_day.resetsAt < now`.
4. Restart the worker (`worker-service.cjs restart`): `rateLimits` becomes `{}`, the first probe after the persisted cooldown succeeds, and every event queued during the outage is lost.

## Expected behavior

- An entry whose `resetsAt` has passed is ignored by the guard (normalise seconds vs ms once in `set()`, see the #3870 thread), and sibling windows are refreshed from `unifiedWindows`.
- Queued observer work survives a graceful restart: drain with a bounded timeout, or persist to SQLite and re-enqueue on boot.
- The SessionStart banner stops telling users that restarting will not help. With the cooldown persisted to `quota-cooldown.json`, a restart is safe and is currently the only fix for Defect 1, but because of Defect 2 it costs the backlog.

## Workaround

`worker-service.cjs restart` after confirming `/api/health` shows an expired `seven_day.resetsAt`. Result here: `Worker restart verified (pid: 53114, version: 13.24.23)`, `rateLimits: {}`, first probe at 23:23:32, 22 observations stored within 6 minutes, 0 quota-guard aborts. The 1297-event backlog was lost.

title: Reject imported rows without memory_session_id instead of aborting the batch
body:
### Problem
`POST /api/import` (fed by `scripts/import-memories.ts` backup restores and
cross-device migrations) declares `observations` / `session_summaries` as
`z.array(z.unknown())` — zero element validation. A legacy or hand-edited export
containing a row with null/missing `memory_session_id` reached
`importObservation` / `importSessionSummary` unguarded, and the SQLite NOT NULL
constraint aborted the ENTIRE import batch.
Observed in the wild: `observer-health.json` 2026-09-01 entry
`"NOT NULL constraint failed: observations.memory_session_id"`.
### Fix
Both importers skip malformed rows with a logged warning and report
`{ imported: false }`, so the rest of the batch proceeds. All other insert
paths were traced and are already guarded at HEAD. Plugin artifacts rebuilt to
carry the same guards (the distributed plugin is what runs in production).
### Testing
- New: `tests/sqlite/session-store-observations.test.ts` (13 tests covering
  per-row rejection, batch continuation, imported:false reporting).
- `bun test` suites: 92 + 57 passing (plugin + core).
- Artifact verification: grep counts for the guard string in built
  SessionStore.js / worker-service.cjs (1/1/1/1).
### Notes for maintainer
- Kept deliberately narrow: no zod route schemas (route also serves
  forward-compat payloads; larger blast radius).
- The plugin-bundle refresh (`61c453ba`) is included so the shipped artifact
  matches; happy to split it into a separate PR if preferred.

body: ## TLDR (for Prioritizer) 1. Research/spec only — three markdown files under `plans/`, no `src/`, no versions, no `/do`, no code plan. 2. The scenario brief (unchanged in substance) stands as overnight research SoT since Alex skipped the PASS widget; its two **lock-next** items now have full specs. 3. **Conflict dedupe lock (scenario 6):** one underlying fact = one node identity in the DOM; applies attach labels, never mint copies. Buckets gain a **restricting** flag: normal labels are OR-allows, restricting labels are AND-gates — deny beats allow, empty result fails closed. Attention trough stays Phase-N, mention only. 6. Ask: PASS the two lock specs; scenario 6/7 OPEN flags and the apply-target table's negation row resolve. title: feat(provider): add openai-compatible provider with an NVIDIA NIM preset
body:
> **Stacked on #3941.** That PR is the first commit on this branch; until it merges the diff here shows both. Review only the second commit (`feat(provider): add openai-compatible provider…`) for this one.

## What this is

`CLAUDE_MEM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` — any endpoint speaking the OpenAI `/chat/completions` shape, on its own settings keys, with presets for NVIDIA NIM, DeepSeek, Groq, Together, Ollama, LM Studio and vLLM.

```json
{
  "CLAUDE_MEM_PROVIDER": "openai-compatible",
  "CLAUDE_MEM_OPENAI_COMPAT_PRESET": "nvidia-nim",
  "CLAUDE_MEM_OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY": "nvapi-..."
}
```

## Why not just `CLAUDE_MEM_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`

That setting already makes the OpenRouter client a generic OpenAI-compatible client, and it keeps working — **nothing on that path changes here**. But it does so from inside a client that carries three things belonging to openrouter.ai and to the cmem.ai gateway specifically:

1. `HTTP-Referer` / `X-Title` attribution headers, sent to whatever host the base URL names. Pointing that at NVIDIA announces claude-mem's OpenRouter leaderboard identity to NVIDIA.
2. `usage: { include: true }`, gated on the URL containing `openrouter.ai` — one special case that has to keep growing per endpoint.
3. The cmem-gateway tuple locking in `resolveOpenRouterConfig`: an intricate and correct set of rules about when a persisted base URL pins a persisted key, so an account-delivered credential is never sent to a host the user just repointed. None of it means anything for a self-configured endpoint, yet a user reaching NVIDIA still has to reason about it, because their config shares the same three settings keys.

So a third-party endpoint gets its own provider id and its own settings, reusing the `OpenAICompatibleProvider` scaffolding and the OpenRouter base-URL normalizer. This gives #2622 (DeepSeek) and #2590 (custom base URL) — both previously answered by pointing `CLAUDE_MEM_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` elsewhere — settings of their own. The local presets ship **no** default model, so nothing is requested that the user did not set, which is the auto-load complaint in #2393. All three are already closed; naming them here is provenance, not a claim to reopen and close them.

## What changed

### New: `src/services/worker/OpenAICompatProvider.ts`

- Concrete provider on the existing `OpenAICompatibleProvider` abstract base.
- Request body is deliberately plain — `model`, `messages`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`, nothing else. Strict servers (vLLM) reject unknown fields, so there is no vendor extra and no usage-accounting flag.
- `classifyOpenAICompatError` leans on status codes and consults the body only for the quota-vs-rate-limit distinction status cannot make. That distinction matters: `quota_exhausted` retires a key for 30 minutes and arms the provider breaker, `rate_limit` for one. A 404 is called out separately and blames the base URL or model, which is what it almost always is on a self-configured endpoint. A failure reported in a 200 body is treated as the equivalent status (the shape #3263 hit).
- Real usage only, both sides or nothing — same rule as `OpenRouterProvider.buildLastUsage`. Token counts are never estimated into the usage event.

### New: `src/shared/openai-compat-presets.ts`

A preset supplies **only** a default base URL and default model; both are overridden by the matching setting, so switching preset never moves an endpoint or model the user pinned. An unknown preset id degrades to `custom` rather than throwing, because settings are read during status polling and a typo must not crash a poll.

### Changed

- `OpenAICompatibleProvider` gains a `requiresApiKey` hook, defaulting to `true` so Gemini and OpenRouter still fail fast. Local servers accept any bearer token or none, so for those an empty key is correct configuration, not an unconfigured provider — and no empty `Authorization` header is sent.
- `provider-dispatch.ts` / `worker-service.ts` / `worker-types.ts` / `quota-cooldown.ts` learn the id. Availability is strict (endpoint + model + key unless local); dispatch falls through to Claude when the provider is selected but half-configured, matching the existing silent fall-through — a misconfigured endpoint should not fail every observation.
- `SettingsRoutes.ts` — **this is a fix, not just wiring.** `validateSettings` checks `CLAUDE_MEM_PROVIDER` against a hardcoded list, and the viewer POSTs the *whole* settings object on every save (`src/ui/viewer/hooks/useSettings.ts`). A provider id missing from that list does not merely hide the option: it `400`s every later save from the settings modal, including saves of unrelated fields. The list and its message gain the new id, with a test asserting every id `getSelectedProvider` can return is accepted.
- `SECURITY.md` — the "content can leave the machine through those channels" list gains this provider. A provider that posts observation context to an arbitrary endpoint belongs there next to `gemini` and `openrouter`.
- `SessionRoutes` takes the new agent as a constructor argument in provider order, which shifts the positional arguments after it; the two tests that construct it directly are updated to match.
- `docs/public/usage/openai-compatible-provider.mdx` + `docs.json` nav.

## Credentials

One credential name (`OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY`) serves every endpoint rather than a per-vendor name, so adding a preset never widens the `EnvManager` `.env` whitelist — that whitelist is a security boundary (#2375).

The `SettingsRoutes` **write** whitelist is deliberately left alone. `POST /api/settings` is unauthenticated (#3680), so `CLAUDE_MEM_OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY` stays settable only from the filesystem or the env. Only the provider *validator* is widened here.

Inherits multi-key rotation via `CLAUDE_MEM_OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEYS` (stacked PR).

## Verified against the live catalog

#3662 was a deprecated default model 404ing out of the box, so the NIM default is not taken on trust: `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` is present in `GET https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/models` as of 2026-09-09 (81 models listed). `api.deepseek.com/v1`, `api.groq.com/openai/v1` and `api.together.xyz/v1` each answer `401` to an unauthenticated `/models`, i.e. the base URLs resolve and require auth as expected. The presets with no default model (`groq`, `together`, and the local three) ship blank on purpose — a model there is not guessable, and `isOpenAICompatAvailable` is false until one is set.

## What this is NOT

- **No installer prompt.** `src/npx-cli/installer-provider-choice.ts` and the `ProviderId` union in `commands/install.ts` do not offer this provider. Settings-file and env configuration work; the interactive flow does not list it. Happy to add it in a follow-up — flagged separately because #3827 is currently reworking that flow.
- **No settings-UI fields.** `ContextSettingsModal.tsx` has no `openai-compatible` option or field block. Left out on purpose: #3433 is already touching that file to surface `CLAUDE_MEM_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`, and a second PR editing the same conditional blocks would conflict. The settings *types* and *defaults* are wired, so it is a UI-only follow-up.
- **Not the server runtime.** `src/server/generation/providers/` keeps its own provider set; `shared/types.ts` `providerLabel` is untouched.
- **Does not fix #3829 items 1–2.** This provider hardcodes `max_tokens: 4096` and inherits `retry.ts`'s 30s `perAttemptTimeoutMs`, exactly as the OpenRouter path does — and a large NIM model will hit that deadline. Making them configurable is one change that should land for *all* providers at once (#3794 / #3808 / #3796 are already on it), not a knob invented here for one provider.
- **No generated bundles.** `plugin/` is untouched — see the stacked PR for why.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck` — clean (both `tsconfig`s)
- `npm run build` — clean, bundle-size guardrails pass
- `bun test tests` — **3183 pass / 27 skip / 0 fail**
- `bun test openclaw` — 44 pass / 0 fail
- `git diff --check` clean; range scanned for `nvapi-` / `AIza` / `sk-or-v1-` / `sk-` shaped strings — none; `docs/public/docs.json` parses
- New: `tests/worker/openai-compat-provider.test.ts` (30 cases). The `accepts every provider id dispatch can select` case was run against the un-widened list and fails without the fix.

> Note for anyone reproducing locally: `Version Consistency > should have version injected into built worker-service.cjs` fails on a bare `bun test tests`, on unmodified `main` too — it needs the build artifact. Run `npm run build` first, as CI does, and it passes.

title: feat(provider): rotate through multiple API keys on rate limit or quota exhaustion
body:
## What this is

Multi-key rotation for the two HTTP providers. `CLAUDE_MEM_GEMINI_API_KEYS` and `CLAUDE_MEM_OPENROUTER_API_KEYS` take extra keys; a key that earns `rate_limit`, `quota_exhausted` or `auth_invalid` goes into a kind-specific cooldown and the next request uses the next key.

Branched off `main` @ `8bc631a`.

## Why

Every provider resolves exactly one API key, and no classified failure re-decides it. A free-tier Gemini or OpenRouter key has a daily allowance measured in a few hundred requests, so an ordinary day of capture spends it before evening — and what happens then is not a slowdown but a stop:

- `rate_limit` is retried twice more against the **same** exhausted key, honoring a `retryAfterMs` that defaults to 60s, so each observation stalls a full minute and then fails anyway.
- `quota_exhausted` and `auth_invalid` are not retryable at all. They throw straight out of `withRetry`, the generator exits, and the quota breaker (#3634) arms the whole provider shut for 30 minutes.

Users answer this today by keeping several free keys and hand-editing `settings.json` when one dies. This closes that loop.

## What changed

### New: `src/shared/api-key-pool.ts`

- `buildKeyPool(primary, list)` — primary key stays index 0; the list is parsed from newline-, comma-, semicolon- or whitespace-separated text, or an array (`settings.json` is hand-edited, and `CLAUDE_MEM_OPENROUTER_MODEL` already tolerates both shapes). Blanks dropped, duplicates collapsed, capped at `MAX_POOL_KEYS = 32`.
- `withKeyPool({poolId, keys}, body)` — runs `body` against the pool, rotating on the three key-fatal kinds.
- Cooldown windows: `rate_limit` 60s (or the endpoint's `Retry-After`, clamped to 1s…15m), `quota_exhausted` 30m (matching `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED_RECHECK_COOLDOWN_MS`), `auth_invalid` 6h. A success clears that key's cooldown immediately, so recovery never waits out a window.

### Wiring

- `GeminiProvider` / `OpenRouterProvider` resolve an `apiKeys` pool alongside the existing `apiKey` and wrap their request in `withKeyPool`.
- `EnvManager` `.env` whitelist gains exactly the two generic plural names (#2375).
- `SettingsDefaultsManager`, `src/ui/viewer/types.ts`, `src/ui/viewer/constants/settings.ts` gain the two settings.
- `docs/public/usage/multi-key-rotation.mdx` + `docs.json` nav; a pointer from each provider page.

## Design notes

- **Rotation wraps `withRetry`, it does not live inside it.** The inner retry keeps owning `transient`; the outer sweep moves on only for the three kinds that mean the key itself is spent. Rotating on a transient failure would spend the whole pool on one flaky network moment.
- **A pool of one key is a pass-through.** The body runs once and nothing is recorded, so single-key installs — which is every install today — keep byte-identical behavior, including which error escapes and when the breaker arms.
- **A fully-spent pool rethrows the LAST classified error unchanged**, so `quota_exhausted` still reaches the breaker (#3634) and `rate_limit` still reaches the pause path (#3760 / #3715). No new error type for callers to learn.
- **When every key is cooling, the nearest-to-expiry key is still tried** rather than failing without sending anything. A misclassification, or an endpoint that reset earlier than it announced, must not become a hard stop.
- **The cmem.ai gateway never pools.** Its key is account-delivered and the `_API_KEYS` list is by definition the user's personal keys, so pooling there would send a personal credential to the gateway — the same leak `resolveOpenRouterConfig` already refuses to commit. There is a test asserting this.

## Credentials

Keys are never written to disk or to a log line, not even truncated. The cooldown file (`~/.claude-mem/api-key-cooldown.json`, mode `0600`, write-then-rename) and every log line carry a per-install salted SHA-256 fingerprint, which is stable within an install and meaningless outside it. This keeps the SECURITY.md "no sensitive data in logs" default true, and is deliberate given #3680 / #3861.

Windows are persisted for the reason `quota-cooldown.ts` already argues: an in-memory-only window is cleared by every restart, and a crash-respawn loop would rediscover each dead key once per restart — the same storm the breaker exists to prevent, one level down. Windows that elapsed while the process was down are dropped on load rather than carried forward.

A rotation logs at `warn` as, e.g.:

```
OpenRouter key 1/3 hit quota_exhausted; rotating to the next key
```

## What this is NOT

- **Not cross-provider failover.** Rotation is within the provider the user selected; `provider-dispatch.ts` is untouched.
- **Not model failover.** #3829 item 3 asks for `CLAUDE_MEM_OPENROUTER_MODEL`'s array form to map onto OpenRouter's native `models[]` fallback instead of being comma-joined. That is the other axis of the same complaint and is **not** addressed here — it is now #3943, filed separately. The two touch adjacent lines in `OpenRouterConfig` and the return of `resolveOpenRouterConfig`, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.
- **Not a timeout or `max_tokens` knob.** #3829 items 1–2 / #3794 / #3808 / #3796 are out of scope.
- **Not the server runtime.** `src/server/generation/providers/` keeps its own providers and its own error classification. The pool reads classified errors *structurally* (`asClassified`) precisely so it can be reused there later without an import cycle, but nothing wires it there in this PR.
- **No generated bundles.** `plugin/` is untouched: a clean `main` already rebuilds those 6 files with ~1,000 lines of minifier-identifier churn, which would bury the diff. Same call as #3882.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck` — clean (both `tsconfig`s)
- `npm run build` — clean, bundle-size guardrails pass
- `bun test tests` — **3153 pass / 27 skip / 0 fail** (this commit alone; 3183 with the stacked provider PR on top)
- `bun test openclaw` — 44 pass / 0 fail
- New: `tests/shared/api-key-pool.test.ts` (33 cases), `tests/worker/provider-key-pool-wiring.test.ts` (9 cases, including the cmem-gateway no-pool assertion)
- `git diff --check` clean; range scanned for `nvapi-` / `AIza` / `sk-or-v1-` / `sk-` shaped strings — none; `docs/public/docs.json` parses
- Every number above was taken with this commit checked out alone — the openai-compatible work is not present.

> Note for anyone reproducing locally: `Version Consistency > should have version injected into built worker-service.cjs` fails on a bare `bun test tests`, on unmodified `main` too — it needs the build artifact. Run `npm run build` first, as CI does, and it passes.

title: Plan: Skill Telemetry — PostHog events for bundled skills
body: Phased make-plan only. No product code. **Plan:** [`plans/skill-telemetry/PLAN.md`](plans/skill-telemetry/PLAN.md) ## Why We cannot see which bundled skills people load. Skill is on the default observation skip list, and no PostHog event fires. ## Az decision (locked) Claude Code `PostToolUse` for the `Skill` tool fires when instructions **load**, not when the work finishes. The plan therefore: - Emits **`skill_loaded`**, not `skill_completed` - Forbids work `duration_ms` from this hook - Keeps Skill off the observation path ## Approach (for a later `/do`) 1. Pure helper: allowlist the 19 plugin skills, else `other` (never send args or third-party names) 2. Whitelist `skill_id` / `skill_source` 3. `captureEvent` on the live worker observation route only (not transcript replay, not server `/v1/events`) 4. Docs that say “loaded,” not “completed” 5. Optional later: SlashCommand undercount, then script-level finish for the 3 skills that have executables ## Not in this PR No instrumentation, no whitelist change, no tests beyond the plan itself. ## Research note Earlier research was written to `skill-telemetry/research-findings.md` in another session; that file is not in this tree. Phase 0 in the plan re-verifies the same facts against current `main`.
